clue.text: Upsetting this trade-off finds you negative — dark but right

indicators.note: upsetting the answer's letters, turning them over into disorder, is what produces the other words, so they are rearranged
but here means except, so the word dark is taken without one of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone finds that disturbing a compromise leaves them gloomy and pessimistic, yet correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: shuffle the answer and you find NEGATIVE plus DAK, which is DARK 'but' (except for) R. So the answer is an anagram of NEGATIVE and DAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise in which each side concedes something is a trade-off, the mutual yielding the phrase describes.

clue.text: What's at the heart of most pleasant summer treats?

indicators.note: the heart is the core, so the outer letters of the word for most pleasant are dropped

parts.note: nicest is the superlative of nice, pleasant

explanation.surface: A question about what makes the best summer treats special.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen desserts such as sorbets are eaten as cooling refreshments in hot weather.

clue.text: Leads to standard for measuring shadows

parts.note: the en is a printer's unit for measuring type width
to shadow someone is to follow, or tail, them

explanation.surface: A measuring standard used for shadows, perhaps on a sundial.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to bring it about as a necessary consequence.

clue.text: Want to do what you'd think doughboys do, as they say

indicators.note: as they say signals that the word is pronounced rather than written

parts.words: do what you'd think doughboys do
parts.note: doughboys sound as though they would work dough, that is knead it

explanation.surface: A wish to behave the way one imagines doughboys behave.
explanation.walkthrough: Doughboys were American infantrymen of World War I (and are also dumplings); the joke is on the 'dough' in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to require or lack it.

clue.text: Check up about secure co-ordinating gear

indicators.note: about places the reversed letters around the word for secure
up in a down clue says the word for check is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to check is to test
to secure a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: An instruction to check that matching equipment is fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check up' reads as a phrasal verb, but in this down clue 'up' turns TEST into TSET, and 'about' wraps that round WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching cardigan and jumper worn together is a classic co-ordinated outfit.

clue.text: Former leader to lay flat House of Lords

parts.note: a knockout in boxing lays the opponent flat
HL is the abbreviation for the House of Lords, the UK upper chamber

explanation.surface: A one-time leader sets out to flatten the upper house of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl was German chancellor from 1982 to 1998, a former national leader.

clue.text: Spirit — reps let it go, being rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A spirit is released by representatives, rum being involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' tempts as the spirit, but here it is the British adjective for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy mischievous ghost is a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Change to the better storm lamp

parts.note: to storm in anger is to seethe
a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: An advertisement for an improved storm lantern, the better model to switch to.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to undergo a conversion, finally understanding and adopting a better view or way of life.

clue.text: A fried option? Laddo moaned, we hear, being out of bed

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken, so their sound is what counts

parts.note: laddo is a term for a lad or sonny, and moaned means sighed
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A breakfast choice, with a young lad grumbling as he gets up.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked on one side only, yolk showing, is one way of serving it fried.

clue.text: Time to list clips — nervous Nerys is on these?

parts.note: to list an item in a register is to enter it
clips and hooks are both fasteners

explanation.surface: Time to put some clips on a list while an anxious woman frets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervous Nerys' is a jocular name for a worrier, who would be on tenterhooks.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on these is an idiom for being in anxious suspense, as a worrier would be.

clue.text: Gold herb, pinch of marjoram, seen in stall — it'll make bangers

indicators.note: seen in places the gold, herb and pinch inside the word for stall

parts.note: a stall in a theatre is a seat
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
sage is a herb

indicators.note: a pinch is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of marjoram is taken

explanation.surface: A recipe of gold, herbs and marjoram at a market stall, for sausage making.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers is British slang for sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced, seasoned pork is the filling stuffed into casings to make sausages.

clue.text: Bishop excused extra duty

indicators.note: excused means let off, so the bishop is dropped from the word for extra

parts.note: a bonus is something extra
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop has been let off some additional duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, a duty laid on someone.

clue.text: Bulgarian accepts what traveller holds back

indicators.note: back says those held letters are read from right to left
the word traveller holds the letters within it, so they are found inside it

explanation.surface: A Bulgarian takes whatever a traveller withholds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulgarian accepts' is a noun phrase: the money Bulgarians accept.
explanation.definitionFit: The lev is Bulgaria's currency unit; this plural form is the money accepted in payment there.

clue.text: Such as could be lost in operations finally

definitions.text: Such as could be lost in operations finally

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of lost in might become something else when rearranged
finally picks the closing letter of operations

explanation.surface: Things that might be removed during surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: these organs are commonly removed in operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Throat glands are often removed by surgery, so they are exactly such things as might be lost in an operation.

clue.text: Grass pulls up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for pulls is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pull is to draw

explanation.surface: Someone yanks grass out of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A sward is an expanse of short grass or turf.

clue.text: Censures stand shown by judges

parts.note: to stand, as in 'let it stand', is to be
to judge the worth of something is to rate it

explanation.surface: Criticism of a position taken by the judiciary.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate is to scold or rebuke angrily, which is to censure.

clue.text: Punt about like a devil

indicators.note: about places the word for punt around the word for like

parts.note: a punt is a wager, a bet
as means like, in the same way

explanation.surface: Someone poles a boat around like a demon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests the flat-bottomed boat; here it is a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruel or monstrous person, or the Devil himself, can be called a brute.

clue.text: West in confusion about eastern kind

indicators.note: about places the shuffled letters around the abbreviation for eastern
letters in confusion are jumbled, so the word West is rearranged

explanation.surface: A chaotic Western scene involving some Eastern type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' rearranges WEST to SWET, and 'about' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet person is kind and gentle in nature.

clue.text: Flood from river near tree

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Water overflows from a river beside a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash of something is a sudden outbreak or flood of it, as in a rash of complaints.

clue.text: Black badger finds crow

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to badger is to pester or tease, which is to rag

explanation.surface: A dark-coated badger comes across a crow.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast or gloat, and so is to brag.

clue.text: Fourth estate stuff

definitions.meaning: the newspapers and journalists, seen as a power in the land
to stuff is to cram or push down tight

explanation.surface: Dismissive talk of the journalists' world.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists collectively are known by this name, and to cram things in tight is also this verb.

clue.text: Monitor Republican stepping down — just the job

indicators.note: stepping down says the Republican letter moves lower in the word for monitor

parts.note: a prefect is a school monitor

explanation.surface: A Republican leaves a monitoring role, which was ideal for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stepping down' moves the R one place later in PREFECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just the job is exactly right, ideal for its purpose.

clue.text: Possibly a crass term for cynicism?

definitions.text: Possibly a crass term for cynicism?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of a crass may be arranged otherwise
a term is a limit or end, so the end of cynicism is taken

explanation.surface: Wondering whether there is a coarse word for cynicism.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting mockery is often rude and cynical, so it might be thought a crude name for cynicism.

clue.text: Provided with object then due

parts.note: an object or aim is an end
money that is due is owed

explanation.surface: Someone is given an item, with payment to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Endowed with means given or furnished with something, such as a quality or funds.

clue.text: Bar a pair involved in academic retiring

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so a and the abbreviation for pair go within the other piece
retiring means drawing back, so the word for academic is read backwards

parts.note: a moot point is academic, of no practical consequence

explanation.surface: Two people get caught up with a shy scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'academic' is in the sense of a moot point, of no practical weight; 'retiring' makes TOOM of it, and 'involved in' sets A plus PR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The public room of a pub where beer is served from the tap is a bar.

clue.text: To shed last of pounds added at the front

indicators.note: added at the front puts that letter before the word for shed
last of picks the final letter of pounds

parts.note: a shed is a hut

explanation.surface: An instruction to a shed: the final pound goes at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is an adverb, as in 'push the door to', meaning closed.
explanation.definitionFit: A door pushed to is pulled closed against its frame, the adverb's sense being closed.

clue.text: Eastern dish starting to track mysterious craft from the south

indicators.note: starting to picks the first letter of track
from the south in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: a UFO is an unidentified flying object

explanation.surface: Tracking an alien craft coming up from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd originates in East Asian cuisine.

clue.text: A passage added on end of one part of church

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is a passage added on to a letter

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of one

explanation.surface: An extra corridor built on to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the rounded or vaulted recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: This predator bowled over divers

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked upside down, so the word for divers is turned round

parts.note: auks are diving seabirds

explanation.surface: A hunting creature knocks over some divers.
explanation.definitionFit: The great skua is a piratical seabird that preys on other birds, an aggressive predator.

clue.text: Whisk porridge

definitions.meaning: to whisk is to mix or beat
porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, time inside

explanation.definitionFit: To beat something round is to mix it; prison slang names both jail and time served this way.

clue.text: They might deliver what gets stuff going?

definitions.text: They might deliver what gets stuff going?

parts.words: They might deliver what gets stuff going?
parts.note: generating stations supply the electricity that makes machines run

explanation.definitionFit: Generating stations produce and deliver electricity, the energy that makes appliances and machinery work.

clue.text: Hide unit which supplies mineral into the bargain

parts.note: an animal's hide with its hair is fur
a therm is a unit of heat
ore is rock from which minerals are extracted

explanation.surface: A deal involving pelts, measured supplies and a mineral source.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the adverb and the idiom mean in addition, besides, as well.
